faq.q: What is the salary of a Customer Service Executive in Bangladesh?
faq.a: Roughly BDT 12,000-25,000 a month for entry level, BDT 25,000-40,000 for mid level, and about BDT 40,000-70,000 for supervisors and managers (an estimate). These ranges combine circulars that show numbers with a salary survey, checked on 16 Nov 2026. Many circulars say negotiable, so confirm in the actual circular.

Most circulars ask for a bachelor's degree in any subject (BBA or marketing preferred in some), clear Bangla, usable English and basic computer skills. Some entry posts accept HSC and many say freshers are welcome.

faq.q: Is Customer Service Executive the same as Call Center Executive?
faq.a: They overlap. Call Center or Contact Center Executive usually means mostly voice work, while Customer Service or Customer Support Executive can also include chat, email and social media. Search all the titles on job sites and read the duties.

faq.q: Will AI replace customer service jobs?
faq.a: Routine work is exposed. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects a 5 percent fall in customer service representative jobs from 2025 to 2035, and The Daily Star reports AI displacing entry-level workers in Bangladeshi BPO. Roles that need empathy, judgement, quality, training and team leading are safer, so build those skills.

faq.q: Do I have to work night shifts?
faq.a: Not always, but 24/7 and international campaigns often have night shifts, for example 10 PM to 8 AM in one circular we saw. Ask about the roster, night transport, allowances and overtime before accepting, and get the answers in writing.

faq.q: Can I get a call centre job abroad?
faq.a: Be extremely careful. Press reports in 2026 describe Bangladeshis lured abroad with promised call centre or data entry jobs and forced to work in online scam compounds. Never pay a fee or hand over a passport to an unverified person, and verify any agency with the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and BMET.

Keep strong quality and satisfaction scores, learn the product deeply, improve your English and writing, help new colleagues, and ask for coaching or quality roles. The typical ladder is executive, senior executive, team leader, supervisor, manager.

faq.q: How do I avoid job scams?
faq.a: Never pay for a job, interview or training seat. Apply through official company pages and verified circulars, be wary of work-from-home offers that ask for upfront money, and report suspicious messages to the Cyber Police Center.

body_md:
**By [Daloyar Hassan Shishir](https://www.dhshishir.com)** · Career consultant, founder of Career Solutions and HereWeGrow · Facts last checked: 16 November 2026

> **Quick answer:** A Customer Service Executive in Bangladesh answers customers by phone, chat, email and social media, solves their problems and records every case. Most circulars ask for a graduate (some accept HSC), clear Bangla, usable English and basic computer skills, and many welcome freshers. Entry pay in the circulars we found is usually BDT 12,000-25,000 a month, mid-level pay BDT 25,000-40,000, and supervisor or manager pay is higher but rarely published. The role is open to AI pressure, so the safe path is to move from routine answers to complex problem solving, retention, quality, training or team leading.

## Customer Service Executive career at a glance

| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| Who hires? | Call centres and BPO companies, banks, telecom and internet providers, mobile finance and fintech apps, e-commerce, ride and delivery apps, hospitals, airlines, and any business with many customers |
| Job titles in circulars | Customer Service Executive, Customer Care Executive, Customer Support Executive, Call Center Executive, Contact Center Executive, Careline Advisor, Customer Excellence Officer (search all of them) |
| Minimum education | Usually a bachelor's degree in any subject (BBA or marketing preferred in some); some entry posts accept HSC, and many say "freshers are encouraged" |
| Must-have skills | Clear Bangla, usable English, listening, typing, patience, basic Word and Excel, comfort with CRM or ticket tools |
| Typical conditions | Shift duty is common, and international or 24/7 centres run night shifts (for example 10 PM to 8 AM) |
| Key rule | Never pay anyone for a job. Never accept a "call centre agent" job abroad from a stranger or an unverified agency |
| Global demand | The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects employment of customer service representatives to fall 5 percent from 2025 to 2035, because of self-service and AI |

## What does a Customer Service Executive do?

A Customer Service Executive is the voice, chat window or inbox of a company. They answer questions, explain products and charges, take complaints, fix what they can, pass on what they cannot, and write down what happened so the next person does not start from zero. In a bank or telecom contact centre the work is mostly inbound calls. In an e-commerce or app company it is chat, email and social media, plus calls to confirm orders. Some circulars mix service with tele-sales, so read the duties carefully.

**A normal day:** log in and check the shift brief, handle calls or chats against a target response time, update the CRM or ticket system after every case, escalate difficult cases with a clear note, call back customers whose issues were pending, join a short team huddle, and finish with a handover. Many posts measure response time, resolution time and customer satisfaction.

> A good reply fixes the problem. A great reply makes the customer feel heard. (our working rule for new agents)

## Scope: where this career can take you

Customer service is a door into several careers:

- **Contact centre ladder:** executive → senior executive → team leader → supervisor → manager.
- **Quality and training:** quality analyst (listens to calls and coaches), trainer, process trainer.
- **Customer success and retention:** keeping customers who might leave, often in software, fintech and e-commerce.
- **Banking service:** customer service officer, relationship officer, branch service desk.
- **Operations and support engineering:** technical support, NOC or service desk, onboarding specialists.
- **Sales and business development:** many agents move into tele-sales, key accounts and partnerships.
- **Self-employed and freelance:** virtual assistant, remote support for foreign clients, your own small support team.
- **BPO sector:** the Bangladesh Association of Contact Center and Outsourcing (BACCO) said at its 2025 summit that its members had created about 85,000 jobs, with a target of 300,000 jobs and USD 5 billion in exports by 2030 (Daily Star; Digibangla). Industry estimates cited by The Business Standard put the whole workforce at roughly 100,000. Treat these as direction, not a guarantee.

## Salary in Bangladesh (2026 ranges)

| Level | Typical experience | Monthly pay (BDT) | Visual |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry | 0-2 years, fresher or first job | 12,000 - 25,000 | ███ |
| Mid | 2-5 years, senior executive or team leader, banks and larger firms | 25,000 - 40,000 | █████ |
| Senior | Supervisor, quality lead, manager (estimate; few public numbers) | 40,000 - 70,000 | ████████ |

**How we got these ranges.** Many circulars say "negotiable", so we used the ones that show numbers, then cross-checked them with a salary survey. Examples from circulars and listings we saw in 2026: a Careline Advisor at Voice Tech Solutions was offered Tk 15,000 a month with a yearly review and two festival bonuses; a Senior Call Center Executive for an international night-shift campaign at 360-Supports was offered Tk 20,000-25,000, with a Tk 2,000 transport allowance, Tk 2,000 attendance bonus and overtime; a Call Centre Representative at EdVerse Global was offered Tk 20,000-25,000; Jatri advertised a contractual Customer Service Executive post at Tk 13,000 plus a Tk 3,000 KPI amount; and Community Bank advertised a Contact Center Executive on a two-year contract at Tk 26,000, asking for one year of contact-centre experience (fresh graduates with strong results could also apply). Small classified ads on Bikroy showed Tk 8,000-12,000. For mid-level, a Sales Support Executive post at Smart Air Bangladesh showed Tk 32,500-37,500. The survey site Paylab reported that 80 percent of Customer Support Specialists earn between Tk 14,480 and Tk 27,329 a month (a survey estimate, not official data). We found no reliable public data for manager-level pay, so the senior figure is an estimate. These are ranges, not promises. Confirm in the actual circular.

### Who pays the most?

As a general pattern: small shops and very small firms → local BPO and general call centres → international and night-shift campaigns, which often add allowances → banks, telecom operators, fintech and large e-commerce companies, which usually offer more structure and a clearer career path. Your own English, typing speed, problem-solving record and any team-leading experience are what move you up.

**Global comparison:** in the United States, the median pay for customer service representatives was USD 44,770 a year (USD 21.53 an hour) in May 2025, with about 2.7 million jobs in 2025 (US Bureau of Labor Statistics). Living costs and the kind of work are very different, so do not compare the numbers directly.

## Benefits beyond salary

- Performance bonus, attendance bonus and overtime, common in call centre circulars.
- Festival bonuses (two a year in several circulars) and a yearly salary review.
- Transport or night-shift allowance in many 24/7 operations, but check it in writing.
- Training in product knowledge, systems and communication, often paid for by the employer.
- A fast first job: many circulars welcome freshers, so you can start earning and learning early.
- A visible ladder in larger companies: executive to team leader to supervisor to manager.
- Transferable skills (communication, handling pressure, record keeping) that employers in banks, sales and operations value.

## Top employers: Bangladesh and the world

**Bangladesh: examples seen in circulars, careers pages or news (alphabetical, not a ranking)**

| Sector | Examples |
|---|---|
| Banks and finance | Community Bank (Contact Center Executive), Midland Bank (customer service posts), many other banks that run 24/7 contact centres |
| Telecom and internet | Grameenphone (customer service and contact centre roles on its careers page), Digi Jadoo Broadband (Officer, Customer Excellence), Alpha Net |
| Fintech and mobile finance | bKash, Pathao (issue resolution and operations roles), POCKET (Trainee Executive, Customer Service) |
| BPO and call centres | 360-Supports, BRAC IT (night-shift customer support for a European logistics client), Voice Tech Solutions |
| Apps, e-commerce and travel | Jatri, Nagorik, Swosti and many online shops |

Always check each employer's own page for current vacancies and conditions.

**A fact worth knowing:** BACCO said outsourcing earnings reached about USD 900 million in the first half of 2025 (The Business Standard), but the same outlet's analysis says wages have stagnated and many young people now see call centre work as temporary. Figures vary by source.

**World:** customer service is one of the largest office occupations worldwide; in the US the biggest employers are retail, insurance and business support services (BLS). Many foreign firms outsource support to Bangladesh, India and the Philippines, and English quality decides who gets those campaigns.

## Skills employers ask for

| Skill | Why it matters | Demand |
|---|---|---|
| Clear Bangla and English speaking and writing | Every call, chat and email | █████ |
| Active listening and empathy | Angry customers calm down when they feel heard | █████ |
| Problem solving and product knowledge | Fewer transfers, faster fixes | █████ |
| Typing speed and accuracy | Chat and CRM work | ████ |
| CRM, ticketing and basic Word and Excel | Named in most circulars | ████ |
| Patience and calm under pressure | Shifts, queues and targets | █████ |
| Escalation and clear note writing | The next person must understand your case | ████ |
| Digital channels: chat, email and social media | Many posts are not voice only | ███ |
| Working with AI tools and chatbots | Agents now handle what the bot cannot | ███ |
| Sales and retention basics | Some roles mix service with tele-sales | ███ |

*Demand bars are our reading of recent circulars, not a statistical survey.*

## Free ways to build these skills

- **HubSpot Academy:** the free [Customer Support course](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses/delivering-exceptional-customer-support) covers handling cases step by step.
- **Coursera:** audit customer service courses for free at [coursera.org](https://www.coursera.org); a paid certificate is optional.
- **Alison:** hundreds of free short courses, including customer service topics, at [alison.com](https://alison.com).
- **Bangla e-learning:** [muktopaath.gov.bd](https://muktopaath.gov.bd) for free national courses, including communication and computer basics.
- **Daily practice:** record yourself explaining one product in Bangla and in English, then listen back and fix filler words and unclear sentences.
- **Typing:** practise with any free typing tool for 15 minutes a day until you can type accurately without looking down.
- **BACCO training:** BACCO announced in January 2026 a plan, with the SICIP skills programme, to train 10,000 young people by 2028. Watch its notices for eligibility (Digibangla).

## Qualifications, licences, scholarships and study support

| Step | Body | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| HSC or bachelor's degree | Any recognised board or university | Most circulars ask for a bachelor's degree in any subject, BBA or marketing often preferred; some entry roles accept HSC |
| Language and typing | Self-study, short courses | Spoken English is often tested in an interview or on a call |
| Company training | The employer | Most centres train you in product, system and script (some pay while you train) |
| Short certificate | HubSpot Academy, Coursera, Alison | Free to learn, helpful proof for a fresher CV |
| Further study | BBA, MBA, marketing, communication | Opens quality, training, management and bank officer routes |
| Professional certificates | ITIL or service-desk certificates | Named as a "plus" in some circulars, for example by BRAC IT, but not required |

**Support to explore (check each official site for current rules):**

- **Chevening (UK):** [chevening.org](https://www.chevening.org) for a funded master's in business, communication or management.
- **Commonwealth Scholarships:** [cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk](https://cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk).
- **DAAD (Germany):** [daad.de](https://www.daad.de/en/).
- **Fulbright (USA):** through the US Embassy in Dhaka.
- **University scholarships:** ask your university about merit and need-based awards for BBA and MBA.

> **Warning on overseas "call centre" jobs:** never pay a "visa fee", "job guarantee" or "training fee" to an individual, and never accept an overseas job offer for a call centre agent, computer operator or typist from an unverified person. Press reports in 2026 describe Bangladeshis lured abroad with promised data entry or call centre jobs and then forced to work in online scam compounds in Cambodia and bdnews24 reported an embassy warning about fake offers for exactly these posts. BMET data show 12,263 Bangladeshis received clearance to travel to Cambodia in 2025. Verify any recruiting agency with the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and BMET before you pay or hand over a passport. Also be careful with "work from home" offers that ask for money upfront for training or equipment (The Business Standard).

## Long-term career timeline

| Years | Typical title | What to master |
|---|---|---|
| 0-1 | Customer Service Executive / Trainee | Product knowledge, scripts, clear speaking, CRM, calm under pressure |
| 1-3 | Senior Executive or specialist (email, chat, escalation) | First-call resolution, difficult customers, quality scores, writing |
| 3-5 | Team Leader, Quality Analyst or Trainer | Coaching, call review, reports, scheduling, simple data analysis |
| 5-8 | Supervisor or Assistant Manager | Targets, staffing, process improvement, customer feedback systems |
| 8+ | Manager, Customer Experience or Operations Lead | Budgets, vendor and technology choices, AI and automation planning |

## Plan your own path (5-minute worksheet)

Copy these five lines and fill them in today:

1. **My level now:** (student / fresher / ___ years in service)
2. **My target role in 3 years:** ___
3. **Three skills I lack** (use the checklist on this page): ___, ___, ___
4. **One learning step this year:** (English course / HubSpot Academy / typing / CRM tool / degree)
5. **My weekly practice hours and day:** ___ hours on ___

Then take the free skill test on this page and compare the result with line 3.

## Career shifts: where Customer Service Executives move

- **Service → quality and training**, if you like coaching and listening to calls.
- **Service → customer success or retention** in software, fintech and e-commerce.
- **Service → sales or business development**, using your skill at understanding customers.
- **Service → banking** (customer service officer or relationship officer).
- **Service → operations, service desk or technical support**, with some technical learning.
- **Service → HR, recruitment or administration**, where communication skills help.
- **Service → freelance or own small business** after you have real experience.

## Where will you find more peace of mind?

We have no survey that ranks the calm of different customer service jobs, so this is a general pattern. Larger companies often have fixed rosters and clearer rules. International and 24/7 campaigns can mean night shifts, which The Business Standard says carry social stigma. Shift work, targets and angry callers are the main pressures. Three habits protect your peace: sleep on a regular schedule even if the shift changes, treat abuse from a caller as the caller's problem, not a verdict on you, and speak to your team leader early when targets feel unfair. Ask about roster, transport at night and overtime before you accept an offer, and get the answers in writing. If stress becomes heavy, talk to a mentor or a mental health professional.

## Faith and history: the weight of a kind word

**The Quran.** "Speak good to people" is a teaching of Al-Baqarah ([2:83 on quran.com](https://quran.com/2/83)). Allah told Musa and Harun to speak gently even to Pharaoh ([20:44](https://quran.com/20/44)). Al-Imran praises gentleness and says harshness drives people away ([3:159](https://quran.com/3/159)). Fussilat teaches to repel an evil with something better ([41:34](https://quran.com/41/34)). These are guides for the hardest calls: stay gentle, stay firm, and answer rudeness with patience.

**Hadith.** The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught that a good word is charity (reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

**History.** Trade in the Muslim world ran on trust and fair dealing, and market inspectors called *muhtasib* checked weights, prices and honesty in the market. Treating the buyer fairly is an old idea, and good customer service is the modern form of it.

## Your contribution to the nation

Every bank, telecom, delivery and payment app depends on people who answer customers well. Good service builds trust in mobile finance, digital payments and online shopping. The BPO sector also earns foreign currency from overseas clients, and BACCO targets USD 5 billion in exports by 2030. A trained, honest, fairly paid workforce means jobs for young people and a more trusted digital economy.

## Your contribution to the world

Bangladeshi agents already support customers abroad, including European and other international clients (for example the night-shift logistics support advertised by BRAC IT). Honest, patient service across time zones improves lives and builds a respected image of the country. As AI takes routine questions, the human contribution moves toward empathy, judgement and fixing what the bot cannot.

## If you want to be an entrepreneur

- **Small support-as-a-service team** for online shops and Facebook sellers (set clear contracts and data privacy).
- **Virtual assistant or remote support** for foreign clients (build a portfolio with proof).
- **Customer service training** for shops, clinics and small businesses (honest, no false guarantees).
- **Chat and social media support agency** for e-commerce pages.
- **Bangla and English chatbot setup** with a human backup, for small businesses.

Start with one real client, keep every promise and register your business as the law requires.

## Research opportunities

- Topics with real need: Bangla speech and chat AI for customer questions, how banks and telecoms measure satisfaction, why agents leave call centres, women and night-shift safety, and which service tasks AI can and cannot do.
- Where to learn and publish: BBA and MBA theses, university business schools, BACCO events and the BPO Summit, and international customer experience journals.
- Path: a BBA or MBA project → customer experience analyst → master's or PhD in marketing, communication or information systems (the scholarships above fund many of these).

## Whom to follow and learn from

Follow organisations first: BACCO for the sector and events, [HubSpot Academy](https://academy.hubspot.com) for free service training, company career pages of banks and telecoms, and The Business Standard and The Daily Star business pages for BPO and AI news. On LinkedIn, follow contact centre managers, quality leads and customer experience professionals who share real examples, and ignore pages that sell "guaranteed job" courses.

## Where to find Customer Service Executive jobs

- [BDJobs](https://www.bdjobs.com) (search the title synonyms above) and company career pages, for example [Pathao](https://careers.pathao.com) and the [Telenor Group career portal](https://www.telenor.com/career/) for Grameenphone roles.
- [Bikroy Jobs](https://bikroy.com/jobs/customer-service-executive) for smaller employers (read pay and company details with extra care).
- [Skill.jobs](https://skill.jobs) and [SmartRecruiters](https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com) pages used by some Bangladeshi companies.
- LinkedIn, and bank and telecom circulars in newspapers.
- Use official company pages or verified circulars only. Do not pay anyone to get an interview or a job.

## Customer Service Executive CV: what to write

Your CV should show communication, numbers and tools, not just "good communicator".

| Weak line | Better line |
|---|---|
| Handled customers. | Handled 60-80 inbound calls a day with a 90 percent satisfaction score (use your real numbers). |
| Good at English. | Wrote email replies in English and completed a free Coursera customer service course (add date). |
| Worked in a shop. | Resolved complaints at a retail counter, reduced repeat visits by keeping a simple case log (use your real example). |

*Use only your real, provable details. Never invent numbers.*

**What to include:** a two-line summary, languages (Bangla and English level), typing speed if tested, tools you can use (Word, Excel, any CRM or ticket tool), shift flexibility if you are willing, any customer-facing work including part-time and volunteering, and certificates with dates.

**Career objective samples:**

- *Fresher:* "Graduate with strong Bangla and English communication seeking a Customer Service Executive role to resolve customer issues politely and accurately."
- *Experienced:* "Customer Service Executive with 3 years in telecom support, consistent first-call resolution and quality scores, seeking a Team Leader role."

Build yours free with the HereWeGrow CV Builder and the Customer Service CV template.

## Common mistakes in applications

- Applying to "Customer Service" and "Telesales" posts without noticing that the work is different.
- Not reading shift, location and contract type before applying (Banani, Khilkhet or Gulshan can mean long travel).
- A CV full of adjectives and no tools, numbers or languages.
- Weak English or Bangla in the CV and cover email itself.
- Accepting a post without asking about roster, night transport, overtime and when salary is paid.
- Paying anyone for an interview, a "training seat" or a job, and accepting overseas call centre offers from strangers.

## Sources and method

Figures were checked on 16 November 2026 and will be reviewed regularly. Pay ranges combine the few circulars that show salary with a survey site and are estimates. Companies change pay and conditions often, so check the actual circular and the employer's own site.

growth_plan.y1: Learn the product and systems deeply, build clear speaking and writing, keep strong quality and satisfaction scores, and avoid job scams.
growth_plan.y2: Move to senior executive or a specialist channel such as email, chat or escalations; improve English and learn a CRM tool well.
growth_plan.y3: Become a team leader, quality analyst or trainer, or move to banking, customer success or sales; build AI and data skills.

goal_sheet: Week 1-2: Record yourself explaining one product in Bangla and English; fix unclear sentences
Week 3-4: Finish the HubSpot Academy customer support course and practise typing 15 minutes a day
Month 2: Learn one CRM or ticket tool through free tutorials and write ten sample case notes
Month 3: Practise mock calls with a friend, with an angry customer and a confused customer
Month 4: Add one chat, email or social media support skill and one basic Excel skill
Month 5: Learn how AI chatbots and agent assist tools work, and note what humans still do better
Month 6: Update CV, write cover letter, apply to 10 circulars, practise 20 interview questions

test.q: A customer is angry about a delayed order. Your best first step is to:
options: Argue that it was not your fault
Listen, acknowledge the problem and apologise for the inconvenience
test.explain: Listening and acknowledging calms the customer and lets you fix the real problem.

options: Answering the first call of the day
Solving the customer's issue in the first contact
test.explain: It measures how often the issue is solved without a repeat contact.

test.q: You do not know the answer to a customer's question. You should:
options: Be honest, check the knowledge base or ask a senior, then call back
test.explain: A wrong answer costs more trust than a short, honest wait.

test.q: After every case, a good executive:
options: Writes a clear note in the CRM or ticket
test.explain: Clear notes let the next person continue without asking the customer again.

test.q: A caller shouts abusive words at you. The best approach is to:
options: Stay calm, set a polite limit and follow the company's abuse policy
Block the number immediately without warning
test.explain: Stay professional, warn politely and escalate as company policy says.

test.q: A stranger offers a call centre agent job abroad if you pay a fee. You should:
options: Refuse, and check any agency with the Ministry and BMET before anything else
test.explain: Fake call centre job offers abroad have trapped Bangladeshis; never pay or hand over a passport to an unverified person.

test.q: Which is the best way to say 'no' to a request the company cannot do?
options: 'I cannot do that, but here is what I can do.'
test.explain: Offer an alternative so the customer still leaves with a next step.
CSAT is a common measure of how satisfied customers were after a contact.

test.explain: Escalate with the facts so the customer does not have to repeat everything.

test.q: A customer shares a PIN or OTP on a call. You should:
options: Never ask for it, tell them not to share it, and follow the security policy
Use it to check the account
Post it in the chat group
test.explain: Genuine staff do not need PINs or OTPs; protect customer data.

test.q: Which opening is best for a Bangla phone call?
options: A greeting, your name, the company and an offer to help
test.explain: A clear greeting sets a polite tone and tells the customer they reached the right place.

test.q: AI chatbots now handle many routine questions. The best career response is to:
options: Build skills in complex problem solving, empathy, quality, training or team leading
test.explain: Routine tasks are the most exposed; judgement and empathy remain valuable.

cv_template_notes: Use the HWG Customer Service CV (clean, one-column layout). Start with a two-line summary, then languages (Bangla and English level), typing speed if tested, tools (Word, Excel, any CRM or ticket system), customer-facing experience with real numbers, shift flexibility if you are willing, and certificates with dates (for example HubSpot Academy). Keep it to 1 page for freshers and 2 pages at most. Use only provable details and never invent numbers. File name: YourName_CustomerService_CV.pdf.

interview_qs: Tell me about yourself. (Tip: 45 seconds: education, languages, one customer-facing example, why this company.)
Why do you want to work in customer service? (Tip: Give a real reason such as helping people solve problems; avoid 'I need any job'.)
Why do you want to work here? (Tip: Name the company's product or service and what you can contribute.)
How would you handle an angry customer? (Tip: Listen, acknowledge, apologise for the experience, fix or escalate, confirm.)
Describe a time you helped someone solve a problem. (Tip: Use a clear structure: problem, action, result.)
What do you do when you do not know the answer? (Tip: Be honest, check the guide or ask a senior, and call back.)
How do you stay calm under pressure? (Tip: Give a real habit such as breathing, short notes or taking a breath between calls.)
Are you comfortable with shift duty and night shifts? (Tip: Answer honestly and ask about roster and transport.)
How do you handle a customer who keeps repeating the same complaint? (Tip: Summarise, confirm understanding and give a clear next step.)
What is first-call resolution? (Tip: Solving the issue on the first contact; explain why it matters.)
What does CSAT mean? (Tip: Customer Satisfaction score.)
How would you say 'no' to a customer politely? (Tip: Say what you cannot do and what you can do.)
Role-play: I am a customer whose bKash or bank transaction failed. Help me. (Tip: Greet, verify identity safely, check, explain, document; never ask for OTP or PIN.)
Role-play: I am a customer who received a damaged product. (Tip: Apologise, collect facts, explain the return steps, set a time frame.)
How fast can you type and how accurate are you? (Tip: Give a real number if you tested it.)
What computer tools do you know? (Tip: Name Word, Excel and any CRM or ticket tool.)
How would you handle three chats at once? (Tip: Prioritise, use saved replies carefully, never copy-paste blindly.)
How do you protect customer data? (Tip: Verify identity, never share PINs or OTPs, keep notes factual.)
What would you do if you made a mistake with a customer's account? (Tip: Tell your supervisor quickly, fix it and prevent a repeat.)
What would you do if a colleague was rude to a customer? (Tip: Support the customer, then raise it respectfully with the team leader.)
How do you handle targets like average handling time? (Tip: Balance speed with quality; never rush a customer in a way that creates another call.)
How do you feel about selling or upselling on a call? (Tip: Answer honestly; say you would only suggest what really helps the customer.)
What do you know about our company's products? (Tip: Do your homework on the website and app.)
How do you think AI will change this job? (Tip: Routine questions go to bots; humans handle complex and emotional cases; say how you will upskill.)
Tell me about a time you worked with a team. (Tip: Show your own contribution, not just 'we'.)
What are your salary expectations? (Tip: Give a range based on the circular and market; stay polite and flexible.)
How soon can you join? (Tip: Be honest about your notice period.)
Where do you see yourself in three years? (Tip: Name a role such as team leader, quality analyst or trainer and the steps you are taking.)
Do you have any questions for us? (Tip: Ask about training, shift roster, performance measures, bonuses and career steps.)
